feedback.problem:
Solve the inequality ${x}^{2}\ge 5x+14$ and express the solution set in interval notation.

$x\in (${{field-1}}$,$
{{field-2}}$]\,⋃\,[$
{{field-3}}$,\,\infty )$
feedback.worked_solution:
To solve this inequality using the graphical method, we first need to move all of the terms to the left-hand side so that the right-hand side is $0.$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2} & \ge 5x+14 \\ {x}^{2}-5x-14 & \ge 0.\end{aligned}
$$

So, we want to find the values of $x$ for which the parabola $y={x}^{2}-5x-14$ lies **above** the $x$-axis or touches this axis. Let's find the roots of the parabola by factoring:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}-5x-14 & =0 \\ (x-7)(x+2) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

We see that the roots are $x=-2$ and $x=7,$ and we can graph the parabola as follows:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14004892/assets/628325ae599d6b004fdabe85319ec9f8acd701c76b776cc4dea6b321cb554415.png)

Since we are interested in solving 

$$
{x}^{2}-5x-14\ge 0,
$$

 
we look for the part of the parabola that is **above** the $x$-axis or touches this axis. 

Based on the graph, the solution is $x\le -2$ or $x\ge 7.$

Using interval notation, we write $x\in (-\infty ,-2]⋃[7,\infty ).$
